lines.en: Hi! **Can I borrow** this book, please?
lines.pt: Oi! Posso pegar este livro emprestado, por favor?

lines.en: Sure! Do you have a library card?
lines.pt: Claro! Você tem cartão da biblioteca?

lines.en: Show me your ID, please. Then you get a card.
lines.pt: Mostre o seu documento, por favor. Aí você recebe um cartão.

lines.en: Here you go. **How long can I keep it?**
lines.pt: Aqui está. Por quanto tempo posso ficar com ele?

lines.en: Three weeks. Please bring it back on time.
lines.pt: Três semanas. Por favor, devolva no prazo.
Qual é a data de devolução?

lines.en: April ninth. It’s on the receipt.
lines.pt: Nove de abril. Está no recibo.

lines.en: Thanks! **Where can I find** cooking books?
lines.pt: Obrigada! Onde encontro livros de culinária?

lines.en: Second floor, on the left. Please talk quietly there.
lines.pt: Segundo andar, à esquerda. Por favor, fale baixo lá.

lines.en: Got it. Thank you so much!

pages.title: Cultural snapshot — Life in the USA
pages.intro: Public libraries are a big part of daily life in many American towns. Look at the cards and guess before you read.

cards.note: Residents can usually get one by showing ID or proof of address.
Most public libraries let you borrow books for free. Many also lend movies and e-books.
Many libraries have quiet areas: you talk softly or not at all.

qs.q: What do you need to borrow a book?
qs.pt: O que você precisa para pegar um livro emprestado?

levels.A2: A library card and sometimes an ID.
levels.B1: You usually need a card, which you get with an ID or proof of address.
levels.B2: Most public libraries issue a free card after you show an ID, and some ask for proof of address as well.

qs.q: What happens when a book is late?
qs.pt: O que acontece se o livro atrasa?

levels.A2: Some libraries ask a small fee.
levels.B1: It depends: some libraries charge a small late fee, and others no longer charge one.
levels.B2: Policies vary: some libraries have removed late fines, while others still charge a small daily fee.

qs.q: How do people behave in a library?
qs.pt: Como as pessoas se comportam numa biblioteca?

levels.A2: They talk softly and turn off the phone sound.
levels.B1: They keep their voice down, but many libraries also have areas where talking is fine.
levels.B2: Quiet study areas exist side by side with spaces for children’s events or group work, where noise is accepted.

pages.compare: In Brazil many public and school libraries also require a registration card. How is it where you live? Is it free?

pages.title: Level up — the same situation from A1 to C2
pages.intro: You do not need six different methods: the structure stays, while language complexity and autonomy grow.

ladder.goal: Ask with words and a gesture.

ladder.say: Can I borrow this book? How long can I keep it?
ladder.goal: Ask permission and the time limit.

ladder.say: I’d like to get a library card, and I want to borrow two books.
ladder.goal: Ask for a service and explain.

ladder.say: Could you tell me whether it’s possible to renew this item online?
ladder.goal: Ask about options with indirect questions.

ladder.say: I’m afraid I’ve misplaced my card; would it be possible to look me up with my ID?
Might I impose upon you to extend the loan, as I’ve not quite finished with it?

pages.note: This progression is illustrative: complex sentences do not define a level on their own. CEFR also considers comprehension, autonomy, fluency, accuracy, interaction and appropriateness.
